name: DOT hazmat placarding requirements by hazard class (any-quantity vs. 1,001 lb threshold)
description: A shipment of hazardous material must be placarded on the transport vehicle, and which placard applies -- and whether it is required at any quantity or only once the aggregate gross weight of that class crosses 1,001 lb (454 kg) -- is fixed by two tables in one regulation, 49 CFR 172.504(e). Table 1's eight categories (explosives 1.1-1.3, poison gas, dangerous-when-wet, temperature-controlled organic peroxide, poison-inhalation-hazard, radioactive) require the named placard regardless of quantity. Table 2's fifteen require it only above 1,001 lb -- but that exception is a highway/rail exception that does not reach bulk packagings, which need a placard at any quantity, so every record carries the general rule and the exception's own scope alongside the number. Each record is one hazard-class / placard pairing. Answers 'do I need to placard this shipment', 'how much of this hazard class triggers a placard', 'which placard goes with hazard class 5.1'.
licence: US federal regulation — 17 USC 105, no copyright
